title: Accenture Pseudocode Mock Test
description: 30 pseudocode / output-prediction MCQs modelled on the reported Accenture pattern: loops with Continue and Jump out of the loop, arrays, recursion, pass-by-reference, and bitwise/increment operators. Conventions: loops include both end values, arrays are zero-indexed, '/' between integers is integer division, 'mod' is the remainder, 'Jump out of the loop' exits the innermost loop, 'Continue' skips to the next iteration. Marking: +1 for each correct answer, no negative marking. Duration: 45 minutes.

questions.question:
Predict the output (loops are inclusive of both ends):

Integer a, b, count
Set count = 0
For (each a from 0 to 5)
    For (each b from 0 to 3)
        If (a > b)
            count = count + 1
        End If
    End For
End For
Print count
questions.explanation: Count pairs with a > b: a=0 gives 0, a=1 gives 1, a=2 gives 2, a=3 gives 3, a=4 gives 4, a=5 gives 4 (b only goes to 3). Total = 14.

questions.question:
Predict the output:

Integer a, b, c, d
Set a = 1, b = 2
For (each c from 1 to 2)
    For (each d from 1 to 3)
        a = a + 2
        If (a > c)
            Continue
        End If
        a = 1
        If (a > d)
            Jump out of the loop
        End If
    End For
End For
Print a + b
questions.explanation: Each pass adds 2 to a, and a (3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13) is always greater than c (1 or 2), so Continue runs every time and the reset a = 1 is never reached. There are 6 iterations, so a = 1 + 6 x 2 = 13 and a + b = 15.

questions.question:
Predict the output:

Integer s, i
Set s = 0
For (each i from 1 to 10)
    If (i mod 3 == 0)
        s = s + i
    End If
End For
Print s
questions.explanation: Multiples of 3 up to 10 are 3, 6 and 9, so s = 3 + 6 + 9 = 18.

questions.question:
Predict the output (integer division):

Integer n, s
Set n = 4825, s = 0
While (n > 0)
    s = s + (n mod 10)
    n = n / 10
End While
Print s
questions.explanation: The loop adds the digits 5, 2, 8, 4: 5 + 2 + 8 + 4 = 19.

questions.question:
Assume the loop increments x by 1 after each pass, and the loop variable can be changed inside the body:

Integer x
For (each x from 0 to 10)
    x = x + 3
End For
Print x
questions.explanation: x goes 0 -> 3 -> (loop adds 1) 4 -> 7 -> 8 -> 11 -> 12. Since 12 > 10, the loop stops and 12 is printed.

questions.question:
Predict the output:

Integer i, j, count
Set count = 0
For (each i from 1 to 4)
    For (each j from 1 to i)
        If ((i + j) mod 2 == 0)
            count = count + 1
        End If
    End For
End For
Print count
questions.explanation: i=1: j=1 (sum 2) gives 1. i=2: j=2 gives 1. i=3: j=1 and j=3 give 2. i=4: j=2 and j=4 give 2. Total = 6.

questions.question:
Predict the output:

Integer i, count
Set count = 0
For (each i from 1 to 20)
    If (i mod 4 == 0)
        Continue
    End If
    If (i * i > 150)
        Jump out of the loop
    End If
    count = count + 1
End For
Print count
questions.explanation: The loop stops at i = 13 (169 > 150). For i = 1 to 12 that is 12 values, minus the multiples of 4 (4, 8, 12) = 9.

questions.question:
What is the output?

Integer a, b, t
Set a = 48, b = 18
While (b != 0)
    t = b
    b = a mod b
    a = t
End While
Print a
questions.explanation: This is Euclid's algorithm: (48,18) -> (18,12) -> (12,6) -> (6,0). It prints the GCD, 6.

questions.question:
What is the output? (The array has 5 elements and changes are made in place.)

Integer arr[5] = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}
Integer i
For (each i from 0 to 3)
    arr[i] = arr[i] + arr[i + 1]
End For
Print all elements of arr
questions.explanation: Each element becomes itself plus the next original element (the next one has not been modified yet): 2+4=6, 4+6=10, 6+8=14, 8+10=18. The last element stays 10.

questions.question:
What is the output?

Integer a[5] = {12, 8, 15, 6, 9}
Integer b[5] = {5, 10, 3, 7, 2}
Integer c[5], k
For (each k from 0 to 4)
    c[k] = a[k] - b[k]
End For
For (each k from 0 to 4)
    Print c[k]
End For

What is the output?

Integer arr[6] = {14, 7, 22, 9, 22, 5}
Integer i, max, pos
Set max = arr[0], pos = 0
For (each i from 1 to 5)
    If (arr[i] > max)
        max = arr[i]
        pos = i
    End If
End For
Print max, pos
questions.explanation: The first 22 at index 2 sets max = 22 and pos = 2. The second 22 is not strictly greater, so pos stays 2.

questions.question:
What is the output?

Integer arr[6] = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}
Integer i, j, t
Set i = 0, j = 5
While (i < j)
    t = arr[i]
    arr[i] = arr[j]
    arr[j] = t
    i = i + 1
    j = j - 1
End While
Print arr[1], arr[4]
questions.explanation: The loop reverses the array to {6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1}. arr[1] = 5 and arr[4] = 2.

questions.question:
What is the output?

Integer arr[7] = {3, 8, 12, 5, 20, 7, 16}
Integer i, s
Set s = 0
For (each i from 0 to 6 step 2)
    s = s + arr[i]
End For
Print s
questions.explanation: Indices 0, 2, 4, 6 hold 3, 12, 20, 16. Sum = 51. (71 is the total of all elements and 20 is the sum of odd indices.)

questions.question:
What is the output?

Integer arr[5] = {2, 1, 3, 1, 2}
Integer i
For (each i from 1 to 4)
    arr[i] = arr[i] + arr[i - 1]
End For
Print arr[3] + arr[4]
questions.explanation: This builds running totals: {2, 3, 6, 7, 9}. arr[3] + arr[4] = 7 + 9 = 16.

questions.question:
What is the output?

Integer m[3][3] = {{1, 2, 3}, {4, 5, 6}, {7, 8, 9}}
Integer i, s
Set s = 0
For (each i from 0 to 2)
    s = s + m[i][i] + m[i][2 - i]
End For
Print s
questions.explanation: Main diagonal = 1 + 5 + 9 = 15. Anti-diagonal = 3 + 5 + 7 = 15. The centre element 5 is counted twice, so the total is 30.

questions.question:
Predict the output of solve(1, 2):

Integer solve(Integer a, Integer b)
    If (a < 3 && b < 4)
        Return solve(a + 1, b + 1)
    Else
        Return a + b
    End If
End Function
questions.explanation: solve(1,2) -> solve(2,3) -> solve(3,4). Now a < 3 is false, so it returns 3 + 4 = 7.

questions.question:
Predict the output of fun(4, 9):

Integer fun(Integer x, Integer y)
    If (x <= 0)
        Return y
    Else
        Return fun(x - 1, y - 1)
    End If
End Function
questions.explanation: Both x and y drop by 1 each call until x = 0: fun(4,9) -> (3,8) -> (2,7) -> (1,6) -> (0,5), which returns y = 5.

questions.question:
What is printed by show(5)?

Function show(Integer n)
    If (n <= 0)
        Return
    End If
    Print n
    show(n - 2)
    Print n
End Function
questions.explanation: It prints 5, 3, 1 on the way down. show(-1) returns immediately, then each call prints its n again on the way back: 1, 3, 5.

questions.question:
What is printed?

Integer f(Integer n)
    If (n == 0)
        Return 1
    End If
    Return n * f(n - 1)
End Function

Print f(5) / f(3)
questions.explanation: f is factorial. f(5) = 120 and f(3) = 6, so 120 / 6 = 20.

questions.question:
What is printed?

Integer sd(Integer n)
    If (n == 0)
        Return 0
    End If
    Return (n mod 10) + sd(n / 10)
End Function

Print sd(9876)
questions.explanation: The function adds the digits: 6 + 7 + 8 + 9 = 30.

questions.question:
What is the output? (&num passes the address, *p accesses the value at that address.)

Function change(Integer *p)
    *p = *p * 3 + 1
End Function

Integer num = 5
change(&num)
change(&num)
Print num
questions.explanation: Because the argument is passed by reference, num itself changes: 5 -> 5x3+1 = 16 -> 16x3+1 = 49.

questions.question:
Assume left-to-right evaluation with post/pre-increment as in Java. What is printed?

Integer a, b, c
Set a = 4, b = 6
c = a++ + --b + a
Print a, b, c
questions.explanation: a++ uses 4 and then a becomes 5. --b makes b = 5 and uses 5. The last a is 5. So c = 4 + 5 + 5 = 14, with a = 5 and b = 5.

questions.question:
What is the output? (& is bitwise AND, ^ is bitwise XOR)

Integer x, y
Set x = 12, y = 10
Print (x & y) + (x ^ y)

What is the output? (<< is left shift, >> is right shift)

Print (5 << 2) - (20 >> 2)
questions.explanation: 5 << 2 = 5 x 4 = 20 and 20 >> 2 = 20 / 4 = 5. The difference is 15.

questions.question:
Assume logical operators use short-circuit evaluation. What is printed?

Integer a, b, c
Set a = 0, b = 5, c = 0
If ((a != 0) && (++b > 5))
    c = 1
End If
If ((a == 0) || (++b > 5))
    c = c + 2
End If
Print b, c
questions.explanation: In the first If, a != 0 is false, so ++b is never evaluated. In the second If, a == 0 is true, so the || short-circuits and ++b is again skipped. b stays 5 and c = 2.

questions.question:
What is the output?

Integer a, b
Set a = 9, b = 14
a = a ^ b
b = a ^ b
a = a ^ b
Print a, b
questions.explanation: Three XOR steps swap two numbers without a temporary variable, so a = 14 and b = 9.

questions.question:
What is the output? (integer division)

Integer num, rev
Set num = 3170, rev = 0
While (num > 0)
    rev = rev * 10 + (num mod 10)
    num = num / 10
End While
Print rev
questions.explanation: The first digit taken is 0, giving rev = 0. Then 7, 1 and 3 give 7, 71, 713. Because rev is an integer, leading zeros disappear, so 713 is printed.

questions.question:
What is the output?

Integer n, i, s
Set n = 28, s = 0
For (each i from 1 to n - 1)
    If (n mod i == 0)
        s = s + i
    End If
End For
If (s == n)
    Print "Perfect"
Else
    Print "Not Perfect"
End If
questions.explanation: The proper divisors of 28 are 1, 2, 4, 7 and 14, which add up to 28. The code tests for a perfect number.

questions.question:
How many vowels does this code count?

String str = "PLACEMENT"
Integer i, count
Set count = 0
For (each i from 0 to length(str) - 1)
    If (str[i] is one of A, E, I, O, U)
        count = count + 1
    End If
End For
Print count
questions.explanation: PLACEMENT has the vowels A, E, E, so the count is 3.

questions.question:
What is the output?

Integer a, b, c, i
Set a = 1, b = 1
For (each i from 1 to 5)
    c = a + b
    a = b
    b = c
End For
Print c
questions.explanation: This generates Fibonacci numbers: c = 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 across the five iterations.
